exercise.instruction: Define class Animal with a method void speak() that prints "Some sound". Define class Dog extends Animal that overrides speak() — include the @Override annotation — and prints "Woof". In main, create a Dog with new Dog(), call speak() on it, and it must print "Woof".
hints: Hint 1: class Animal { void speak() { System.out.println("Some sound"); } }
Hint 2: class Dog extends Animal { @Override void speak() { System.out.println("Woof"); } }
Hint 3: In main: Dog d = new Dog(); d.speak();

quiz.question: Which keyword makes a class inherit from another?
What does @Override do?
options: Tells the compiler this method replaces a parent method

quiz.question: Animal a = new Dog(); a.speak(); — whose speak() runs?
